symptom: POST /orders returns HTTP 500 after inventory reservation.
evidence: Trace 6b2d4f8a1c3e5d7f: inventory.reserve returned 409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK; order.persist was not called.
Release v1.0.1 changed inventory reservation from a pre-check to an atomic reserve call.
root_cause: The order service maps an expected inventory reservation conflict to an unhandled server error.
expected_findings: Inventory reservation returned 409
Order persistence was not reached
The error mapping changed in v1.0.1
safe_next_step: Review the conflict-to-HTTP mapping and confirm the intended client response before changing production behavior.

symptom: POST /orders latency rises and requests return HTTP 500.
evidence: Trace 7c3e5a9b2d4f6a8c: db.acquire waited 5000 ms and timed out.
Database reports 20 active connections, equal to configured pool maximum; no database errors are recorded.
root_cause: The application's database connection pool is exhausted and acquisition times out.
expected_findings: Connection acquisition timed out
Pool is at its configured maximum
Evidence does not show database unavailability
safe_next_step: Inspect connection checkout duration and release paths, then evaluate pool sizing against database limits.

symptom: Newly deployed instances return HTTP 500 on order writes.
evidence: Trace 8d4f6a0c3e5b7d9f: INSERT failed with column 'delivery_window' does not exist.
Release v1.2.0 added delivery_window to the ORM model; database migration event is absent in the release window.
root_cause: Application code was deployed before the schema change that adds delivery_window.
expected_findings: The database rejected a missing column
Application release expects delivery_window
No migration event was found in the observed window
safe_next_step: Verify migration status and deployment ordering with the database owner before applying a schema change.

symptom: Checkout requests fail after approximately three seconds.
evidence: Trace 9e5b7d1f4a6c8e0b: payment.authorize ended with upstream timeout after 3000 ms.
The same trace shows inventory.reserve completed in 42 ms and order.persist was not reached.
root_cause: The payment authorization dependency timed out before order persistence.
expected_findings: Payment authorization timed out
Inventory reservation succeeded
Order persistence was not reached
unsupported_claims: The payment provider is globally down
safe_next_step: Check the payment provider's status and retry policy; verify idempotency before retrying authorization.

symptom: Requests fail before connecting to the payment dependency.
evidence: Trace a06c8e2b5d7f9a1c: payment client raised EAI_AGAIN for payments.internal.
No TCP connection or TLS handshake span exists for that dependency.
root_cause: The runtime could not resolve the payment dependency hostname.
expected_findings: DNS resolution returned EAI_AGAIN
Failure happened before connection establishment
unsupported_claims: The payment API returned an HTTP error
safe_next_step: Check resolver health and service discovery for the affected runtime before restarting workloads.

symptom: Outbound payment requests fail during TLS setup.
evidence: Trace b17d9f3c6e8a0b2d: TLS handshake failed with certificate has expired.
DNS resolution and TCP connection to payments.internal succeeded.
root_cause: The certificate presented by the payment endpoint was expired at connection time.
expected_findings: TLS handshake reported an expired certificate
DNS and TCP connection succeeded
unsupported_claims: The application trust store is corrupt
The certificate belongs to a specific owner
safe_next_step: Verify the presented certificate chain and coordinate renewal with its owner.

symptom: Order reads fail while the primary database remains responsive.
evidence: Trace c28e0a4d7f9b1c3e: cache.get failed with ECONNREFUSED at redis.internal:6379.
The health query to the primary database completed successfully in 18 ms.
root_cause: The order service cannot connect to its Redis cache endpoint.
expected_findings: Redis connection was refused
Database health query succeeded
The evidence isolates the observed failure to cache access
safe_next_step: Check Redis service health, endpoint routing, and recent configuration changes.

symptom: Queued fulfillment jobs increase while completion rate drops to zero.
evidence: Worker log: process exited with code 1 after deserialization error for message schema version 4.
Queue depth increased from 12 to 87 in ten minutes; no successful completion event appears in that interval.
root_cause: The worker cannot deserialize the newly observed message schema and exits.
expected_findings: Schema version 4 deserialization failed
Worker exited with code 1
Queue backlog grew during the interval
unsupported_claims: All queued jobs are permanently unrecoverable
A producer deployment caused it without release evidence
safe_next_step: Compare producer and consumer schema compatibility; preserve queued messages while investigating.

symptom: Order creation fails after database commit when publishing an event.
evidence: Trace d39f1b5e8a0c2d4f: order.persist succeeded; event.publish returned 403 ACCESS_REFUSED.
Broker response identifies exchange orders.v2 and the authenticated principal lacks write permission.
root_cause: The broker denied the application's publish request because the principal lacks write permission on orders.v2.
expected_findings: Order persistence succeeded
Publish was denied with 403
Broker identifies a missing write permission
unsupported_claims: The user should receive a retry without checking duplicate handling
safe_next_step: Have the broker owner review the principal's least-privilege binding and reconcile the committed order before retrying.

symptom: Payment authorization calls receive a burst of upstream 429 responses.
evidence: Trace e4a02c6f9b1d3e5a: payment.authorize returned HTTP 429 with Retry-After: 30.
Requests were sent at 45 per second; configured client limit is 50 per second.
root_cause: The upstream payment provider rate-limited requests under its own quota policy.
expected_findings: Provider returned HTTP 429 and Retry-After 30
The trace does not identify an application-side 50-per-second limit breach
unsupported_claims: The provider quota is exactly 40 requests per second
Payments were declined by card issuers
safe_next_step: Honor Retry-After and confirm the provider quota and idempotent retry behavior.

symptom: Payment requests begin returning HTTP 401 after credential rotation.
evidence: Trace f5b13d7a0c2e4f6b: payment.authorize returned 401 INVALID_API_KEY.
Secret rotation event completed at 10:02 UTC; failing process reports credential version v17, while the secret store reports current version v18.
root_cause: The running process is using a stale payment credential after the secret store rotated to v18.
expected_findings: Provider rejected the credential
Runtime uses v17 while store current version is v18
Rotation preceded the failure
safe_next_step: Verify secret refresh behavior and rollout status without printing credential values.

symptom: Requests fail when the service writes temporary export files.
evidence: Trace 06c24e8b1d3f5a7c: write /tmp/order-export.tmp returned ENOSPC.
Container filesystem usage is 100%; persistent database storage reports 61% usage.
root_cause: The container's writable filesystem is full, preventing temporary file creation.
expected_findings: Temporary file write returned ENOSPC
Container filesystem is full
Database storage is not full in the supplied evidence
safe_next_step: Identify safe temporary-file cleanup or capacity remediation with the service owner; do not delete unknown files.

symptom: The service restarts during large order report generation.
evidence: Runtime event: container terminated with reason OOMKilled, exit code 137.
Memory usage reached the 512Mi container limit during report.render; CPU remained below its limit.
root_cause: Report generation reached the container memory limit and the runtime killed the process.
expected_findings: Container was OOMKilled with exit code 137
Memory reached 512Mi during report.render
CPU limit was not reached in the supplied sample
unsupported_claims: The node ran out of memory
Increasing the limit alone will fix the root cause
safe_next_step: Profile report memory use and compare workload size with configured resource limits.

symptom: Request latency rises while the service remains available.
evidence: Trace 17d35f9a2c4e6b8d: request spent 2.4 s in local JSON serialization; database span took 21 ms.
Container CPU throttling increased to 72% of periods; CPU limit is 500m.
root_cause: CPU throttling is consistent with the prolonged local serialization span under the configured CPU limit.
expected_findings: Long time is in local serialization, not the database span
CPU throttling is elevated
Evidence supports correlation, not a proven code-level cause
unsupported_claims: A specific serialization bug is proven
safe_next_step: Profile serialization CPU cost and compare representative payload sizes before changing limits or code.

symptom: Only requests taking the new discount path return HTTP 500.
evidence: Trace 28e46a0b3d5f7c9a: discount.calculate raised TypeError because discount.rules was null.
Feature flag new-discount-flow is enabled for 10% of requests; control-path traces succeed.
root_cause: The enabled discount path receives a null rules configuration and raises a TypeError.
expected_findings: Null discount.rules caused the observed TypeError
Failure is associated with the new-discount-flow path
Control traces succeeded in the supplied sample
unsupported_claims: The feature flag rollout caused every failure
The configuration is null for all tenants
safe_next_step: Validate the flag-scoped configuration and inspect the affected cohort before changing flag exposure.

symptom: Authenticated requests lose tenant context behind the new gateway.
evidence: Trace 39f57b1c4e6a8d0f: gateway forwarded X-Tenant-ID; middleware read x-tenant-id from a case-sensitive custom map and returned missing tenant.
Direct requests bypassing the gateway include the lowercase key and succeed.
root_cause: Middleware tenant-header lookup is case-sensitive while the gateway forwards a differently cased header name.
expected_findings: The forwarded header casing differs from the lookup key
The middleware reports missing tenant
Direct lowercase-header requests succeed in the sample
unsupported_claims: The identity provider rejected the user
safe_next_step: Review case-insensitive header handling and add a regression test for gateway-forwarded requests.

symptom: Product lookup load and latency spike after a cache key expires.
evidence: Trace 4a06c82d5f7b9e1a: 184 concurrent requests for product:SKU-42 all missed cache within 100 ms.
Database query count for that key rose from 1 to 184; individual queries completed in 180-210 ms.
root_cause: Concurrent cache misses for the same expired key caused a burst of duplicate database reads.
expected_findings: 184 requests missed the same key concurrently
Database reads increased to 184 for that key
The supplied evidence shows elevated load, not database failure
unsupported_claims: A lock implementation is already deployed
safe_next_step: Assess request coalescing or stale-while-revalidate options and validate cache consistency requirements.

symptom: Signed payment requests are rejected although the key identifier is accepted.
evidence: Trace 5b17d93e6a8c0f2d: provider returned 401 SIGNATURE_EXPIRED.
Runtime clock is 94 seconds ahead of the time source; provider allows 30 seconds of clock skew.
root_cause: Runtime clock skew exceeds the provider's signature validity tolerance.
expected_findings: Provider rejected an expired signature
Runtime skew is 94 seconds
Provider tolerance is 30 seconds
safe_next_step: Check time synchronization on affected runtimes and verify timestamps without exposing signature material.

symptom: Some payment attempts have duplicate authorization records after transient timeouts.
evidence: Trace 6c28e04f7a9b1d3e: first authorization timed out waiting for response; retry used a new idempotency key.
Provider query shows two authorization IDs for the same order reference, both currently authorized.
root_cause: The retry generated a new idempotency key after an ambiguous timeout, allowing a second authorization.
expected_findings: Initial result was ambiguous due to timeout
Retry used a different idempotency key
Provider returned two authorized records for the order reference
unsupported_claims: The provider created records without a client retry
safe_next_step: Stop automatic retries for this case and reconcile both authorization IDs with the payment owner.

symptom: HTTP 500 rate rises immediately after release v2.4.1.
evidence: Release event v2.4.1 at 14:02 UTC changed src/orders/mapper.ts.
Trace 7d39f15b0a2c4e6f at 14:04 UTC: mapper.readAddress raised Cannot read properties of undefined; v2.4.0 traces use the previous mapper successfully.
root_cause: The changed address mapper in v2.4.1 is associated with the observed undefined-value exception.
expected_findings: The exception occurs in mapper.readAddress
The release changed the mapper shortly before the error
The trace supports a release correlation
unsupported_claims: The release is conclusively the only cause
safe_next_step: Compare the changed mapper behavior with failing input and route any rollback through the release approval process.
